workspaces caught up. Now workspace fetch only triggers on its own

fix: prevent duplicate inserts via version counter, auto-chain batched inserts

Three fixes for write_to_pad duplication bug:

1. Version counter: server tracks a monotonic docVersion that bumps on every
   agent write. Browser includes its last-seen version in doc-update messages.
   Server rejects stale doc-updates that would overwrite agent changes.
   Replaces the fragile 3s time-based lock as the primary safety mechanism.

2. Auto-chain batched inserts: when multiple inserts in the same batch target
   the same afterNodeId, the server auto-redirects subsequent inserts to chain
   after the previously inserted node. This preserves array order in the
   document (first change in array = first in document).

3. StrictMode WebSocket fix: detach onclose handler before intentional close
   in cleanup, preventing a phantom reconnect timer from creating duplicate
   connections.

Also adds dedup check in bridge.ts batched insert path as defense-in-depth.

fix: resolve orphaned imageLoading placeholder in insert_image

Three fixes for the imageLoading node persisting after image generation:

1. mcp.ts: Phase 2 now hard-replaces imageLoading by TYPE (not stale ID)
   and broadcasts document-switched instead of using applyChanges. During
   async generation (5-10s) the agent lock expires and browser doc-updates
   can change node IDs, making the original loadingNodeId stale.

2. ws.ts: Strip imageLoading nodes from incoming doc-updates. They're
   ephemeral placeholders that should never survive a round-trip.

3. apply.ts: Use single tr.replaceWith() instead of chained deleteRange +
   insertContentAt for rewrites. The chain has position mapping bugs for
   atom nodes (nodeSize=1).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix: break infinite render loop in TweetEditor from unstable onReady callback

TweetEditor's onReady useEffect depended on [editor, onReady], but onReady
was an inline arrow function from TweetComposeView that changed every render.
This caused: effect fires → handleEditorReady → onEditorsChange → setAllEditors
(new array ref) → App re-renders → TweetComposeView re-renders → new onReady
→ effect fires again → infinite loop.

Fix: use useRef for onReady so the effect only depends on [editor].

fix: re-set agent lock before tweet thread HR resync

When inserting new tweets (HR + paragraph) into a thread, the server
sends document-switched to trigger a full resync. The browser recreates
all tweet editors, each firing onUpdate → stale doc-update. The original
3s agent lock expires before the browser finishes recreating editors.

Fix: re-set the lock right before sending document-switched so the 3s
window starts from when the browser receives the new state.

fix: use twitter-text weighted counting for tweet character limits

(日 = 1 vs correct 2), URLs counted by actual length (vs fixed 23).

26px circle crowds 3-digit counts and minus signs against the edge.
Now grows to 30px when numbers are visible (≤20 remaining), and
shrinks font to 10px for 2+ digit values.

Adds syncPostHistory() that fetches scheduler_history from platform,
matches by doc_id, writes lastPost metadata to local doc frontmatter.
Runs on: server startup, schedule sidebar open. Platform is canonical
for post state; frontmatter is cached view for sidebar display.

handleDelete now checks response and awaits fetchConnections.

compatibility.

wip: schedule_post handles threads — splits at horizontalRule, uploads images per tweet

Detects thread docs (horizontalRule separators), splits into tweet
array, extracts text + images per tweet, uploads images per tweet,
queues as content_type "thread" with tweets array. Single tweets
unchanged.

wip: schedule_post extracts images and uploads via platform

schedule_post now finds image nodes in TipTap doc, reads files
from disk, uploads via platform's /connections/:id/upload-media
endpoint, and includes mediaIds in queue content. Also adds
proxy route for upload-media.

wip: schedule_post reads from active doc, no content param needed

Document is canonical — schedule_post reads content + content_type
from the active doc automatically. Agent just calls schedule_post
with optional mode/connection_id/slot_id. Platform queue stores
content snapshot; documents store zero scheduling metadata.

Splits multi-day slots into per-day slots with randomized time
offsets so scheduled posts don't look automated. Creates
deterministic jitter per day/slot combination.

falling back to text-only for unsupported browsers.
